note: The plain What's new notes, one entry per release since 1.14.0, newest first: the popup after an update, Settings > Advanced > What's new and Dalamud's installer listing (tools/make_pluginmaster.py) read them. Written for players: 3 to 5 points, each a short lead and one plain sentence, no class names, settings paths only when the player needs them, no lists of fixes. CHANGELOG.md stays the technical record. Add the new release's entry before tagging it; the tests fail when the csproj version has none.

points.text: A peg game under Menphina's moon: open it with the Moonfall button on the main window or /tsuki moonfall. This preview has The Moon Road's first two stages, ten levels; more of the road is on its way.
Eleven familiar faces lend their powers when you hit a green peg, shown on their Triple Triad cards.
Every level is drawn over a night scene, from the Thanalan roads to the twin lanterns of Vesper Bay, using the game's own art from your install.
Moonfall follows your spoiler shield: places and companions your story hasn't reached stay hidden until you get there.
This is a preview, so levels, scores and balance may change before the full release.
Quest-giver portraits were re-cut by hand so faces sit in the middle, and each quest shows a character as they looked at that point in the story.
Quest-giver photos now come with Tsukimichi, so there's nothing to download. Turn them off in Settings, under Look.
Click a column header in Moonlit to sort by it; click again to reverse.
If you use Umbra, Tsukimichi can put its widget on your Umbra bar for you, and take it off again.
After each update, a short note like this one shows what changed. Past notes are in Settings, under What's new.

points.lead: Know when an update is ready.
points.text: A quiet note in the status bar and a dot on the moon icon tell you. Update opens Dalamud's installer.
A small moon opens Tsukimichi and shows what's next when you hover it. Move it, lock it or hide it.
Tsukimichi offers the optional portrait pack once. Nothing downloads unless you choose Download.
Tsukimichi keeps clear of Umbra's toolbar, and an Umbra add-on puts Tonight in your Umbra bar.
Tonight starts with one suggestion for the character you're on, and says why.
Travel aims at the step you're on, not only at the quest giver.
One board shows each character's story, goals and what's Ready.
Storylines you started and never finished, finales first.
Past where you are in the story, Tsukimichi now hides the names of places, duties, rewards and people too. Hover a hidden name to see why.
A card in Tonight lists what each character should finish before Patch 8.0: the story, journal room, job quests, roulettes and flying. Tick lines off as you go.

points.lead: More faces, if you want them.
points.text: An optional download adds about 1,850 quest-giver portraits. Nothing downloads until you choose it in Settings › Look.

points.lead: The game has the last word.
points.text: When the game offers you a quest, Tsukimichi shows it as Ready, even one it couldn't check before.
Quests with a duty say whether NPCs can come along or you need a group, and which job gets the most from the EXP.
See how full your journal is, and what you can finish or safely drop to make room.
Seasonal events warn you three days before they end, and their quests come first.
Search for "Kugane" or "flying Thavnair" to see the quests that open it, with a route there.
When a run stops, a card says why in plain words and offers a safe way to carry on.
If you're knocked out, stuck, or your duty pops during a run, one calm panel and a sound tell you.
Questionable no longer walks you into a duty with other players unless you say so.
Stop a run after this quest, after a few more, or at a time you choose.
Pick a level of automation, from tracker only to full hand-offs, in Settings › Automation.
Astrologian's Orrery and Sumi to Kinpaku join the list, with two new palettes, Dawn and Kugane Lacquer.
Pick each quest state's moon from any theme, and Tsukimichi warns you when two would look alike.
Brass, silver, lead, astrolabe or gold-leaf rims go with any theme.
Copy your look as a short code, or paste a friend's to see it before you apply it.
Settings › Themes offers Menphina's Medallion, Ishgard Glass, Aether Crystal and Classic. Hover a card to preview it.
Ishgard Snow is a light palette with navy ink and a still dawn sky.
High contrast has its own designed look, with every word easy to read.
Reset appearance returns to the usual look, and Undo is there if you change your mind.
The Giver card shows who to walk up to, from the game's own art, and never a face from story you haven't reached.
Next stops, the Route window and the Todo overlay show a small portrait of each giver.
Travel buttons, requirements, duties and your characters' progress wear the icons you know from the game.
Step back through the quests you looked at with the ‹ › buttons, your mouse's side buttons or Alt and the arrow keys.
The stars twinkle and drift, and a shooting star marks each quest you complete.
Settings shows a fingerprint of the plugin you're running, so you can compare it with the release.
Section names and the Journal's column headers are larger and brighter, and the filters fit their space.
The Journal badge counts the quests that became Ready since you last looked.
